[Big Step!] Russia and Ukraine Agree to a [Large Prisoner Swap] After Abu Dhabi Talks
caption:
🕊️ Russia and Ukraine agree to a large prisoner swap

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war after two days of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, both sides said on Wednesday. These were the first direct talks between the two countries in nine months.

🔹 The swap was confirmed by Russia's chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky and Ukraine's Rustem Umerov. The exact numbers are still being finalised.
🔹 US envoy Jared Kushner called it the "biggest humanitarian release of prisoners" of the war.
🔹 No deal was reached on a ceasefire, territory or security guarantees. US envoys Kushner and Steve Witkoff then met President Putin in Moscow and President Zelensky in Ireland, and say a new round of talks is planned.

headline: [Global Outage!] Microsoft Outlook and Teams Go Down for [5+ Hours]
sub: Over 138,000 problem reports at peak
caption:
💻 Microsoft Outlook and Teams down for hours

A major Microsoft 365 outage disrupted Outlook email, Teams and other Microsoft services for more than five hours on Thursday, Reuters reported. Problems began around 12:30 p.m. US Eastern time, and Microsoft said users in any region could be affected.

🔹 Problem reports for Outlook on Downdetector peaked at more than 138,000, according to Reuters.
🔹 Microsoft said a number of servers became unexpectedly unavailable because of elevated load, mainly hitting Exchange Online email.
🔹 Microsoft said it was returning servers to service and moving traffic, and warned that recovery would be gradual as users reconnect.

headline: [Tensions Rise!] Iran Says It Hit a [US Radar] in Bahrain
sub: The claim has not been independently verified
caption:
⚠️ Iran Says It Hit a US Radar in Bahrain

Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) said on Friday that they targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. Iran's state news agency IRNA reported the statement. AP and Al Jazeera said the claim could not be independently verified, and the US and Bahrain did not comment straight away.

🔹 The IRGC said it was a reply to an attack on a telecom tower in Sirik, a port city in southern Iran, on Thursday.
🔹 According to Reuters, it is Iran's first claimed attack on US military assets in a Gulf country since early September.
🔹 Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. The IRGC warned it is ready to act again.

💬 Do you think talks can stop the tension from growing? 👇

sub: Huang agrees to testify before Congress
caption:
💻 Trump says Tim Cook should lead Nvidia

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Apple's Tim Cook should become the new CEO of Nvidia, after Jensen Huang stepped down. In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote that there is "only one man" to take Huang's place and called it "A Legend replaces a Legend!"

🔹 Nvidia has named its finance chief, Colette Kress, as interim CEO while its board looks for a permanent leader.
🔹 Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO in September and is now executive chairman of Apple's board.
🔹 Huang has agreed to testify before US lawmakers in a closed-door session by Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs Committee chairman Brian Mast said.

caption:
🌎 Trump Says He Wants to "Get Cuba Done" Before Leaving Office

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he wants to "get Cuba done" before he leaves office in 2029. Speaking in a radio interview with host Hugh Hewitt, he said he would consider using military force against Cuba and that his team is "watching it very closely."

🔹 Politico reported this is the first time Trump has given a timeline for possible action on Cuba.
🔹 Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio, whose parents are from Cuba, "would love to do it."
🔹 Since January, the US has blocked most oil shipments to Cuba, which has led to blackouts and food and fuel shortages. Cuban officials have said the island is ready for any attack.

🏏 India All Out for 89 as New Zealand Win by 244 Runs

New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday. New Zealand made 333, and India were bowled out for just 89 in reply.

sub: Up to 1 million expected at his Mass
caption:
🙏 Pope Leo Returns to the Peru City He Led as Bishop

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Chiclayo, Peru, on Friday for an outdoor Mass in the city where he served as bishop for eight years. Local officials said up to 1 million people could attend.

🔹 Before becoming pope, Leo (born Robert Prevost in Chicago) worked in Peru for about 20 years as a missionary priest and bishop.
🔹 In Lima on Wednesday, about 3 million people came out to see him, the biggest crowd of his papacy so far, Reuters reported.

headline: [Massive Attack!] Ukraine Fires Nearly [1,200 Drones] at Russia Overnight
sub: Russia says it shot down 1,198 drones
caption:
⚠️ Ukraine Fires Nearly 1,200 Drones at Russia Overnight

Ukraine launched almost 1,200 drones at Russia overnight from Thursday to Friday, one of its biggest air attacks since the full-scale war began nearly five years ago. Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences shot down 1,198 drones over more than 15 regions.

🔹 Russian officials reported deaths. At least four workers were killed in an industrial area in the Volgograd region, the regional governor said.
🔹 Moscow's mayor said 467 drones were heading for the capital. Russia also attacked Ukraine overnight; Ukrainian officials said at least two people were killed in Odesa.
🔹 The attack came after two days of US-led talks in Abu Dhabi. US envoys say Europe will join the next round of peace talks.

sub: Senate probe into AI chips reaching China
caption:
💻 Nvidia Scandal Grows: US Commerce Chief Lutnick Agrees to Testify Before Senate

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee, CNN and CBS News reported on Friday. The committee is looking at how advanced Nvidia AI chips may have reached China, and why the US did not act sooner.

🔹 Committee chairman Senator Tim Scott asked Lutnick to testify on December 10. A source said the details are still being worked out.
🔹 The probe centres on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer that US officials suspect of helping Chinese firms get around chip export limits. China rejects the spying claims linked to the case.
🔹 Lawmakers have also asked former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned this week, to testify in early December, and warned they could use subpoenas.

headline: [Rare Shutdown!] US Grounds Flights Nationwide for [4+ Hours]
sub: Air traffic communication failure halts departures
caption:
✈️ Rare Shutdown: US Grounds Flights Nationwide for 4+ Hours

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) stopped flights from taking off at all US airports on Friday afternoon, after a communication problem hit air traffic control centres across the country. Departures were halted for more than four hours before the FAA lifted the order late Friday.

🔹 The FAA said the ground stop was ordered "for reasons of safety" after "communication issues" at multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers. Technicians are still looking into the cause.
🔹 By Friday evening, FlightAware showed more than 1,900 flights cancelled and over 10,000 delayed in the US. Delays are expected to continue.
🔹 Officials said there was no sign of a "nefarious" act. It was the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023.

headline: [Health Setback!] US Reportedly Loses Measles-Free Status After [26 Years]
sub: Measles kept spreading for over a year
caption:
🦠 Health Setback: US Reportedly Loses Measles-Free Status After 26 Years

The United States has lost its "measles eliminated" status, which it held since 2000, according to reports by Reuters and CNN on Friday. Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, said the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) took the step because measles kept spreading in the US for more than a year.

🔹 The CDC had counted 5,182 confirmed measles cases in 2026 as of Thursday, from 45 states, New York City and Washington, D.C. That is more than double the 2,289 cases in all of 2025.
🔹 State health officials have reported at least 10 measles-related deaths in the US this year, after two more were reported in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin.
🔹 PAHO and the US health department had not commented publicly when the reports came out. Experts say two doses of the measles vaccine give about 97% protection.

caption:
⚽ Post-Messi Era Begins: Uruguay Beat Argentina 2-1 at La Bombonera

Uruguay beat Argentina 2-1 in a friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires on Friday night. It was Argentina's first match since Lionel Messi retired from international football in early October.

🔹 Uruguay scored twice early in the second half: a Leonardo Balerdi own goal (48') and a goal by Maxi Araújo (53'). Julián Álvarez pulled one back for Argentina in the 73rd minute.
🔹 Argentina left the No. 10 shirt unassigned. Coach Lionel Scaloni said: "We have to rebuild without Leo Messi, and we have the talent to bounce back from this loss."

sub: Iran says ships used banned routes
caption:
🚨 BREAKING: Iran Says 3 Oil Tankers Hit Mines and Caught Fire in Hormuz

Iran's navy and Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that three oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire. Iran says the ships had switched off their tracking systems and were using routes it does not allow.

🔹 Iran said two of the tankers were hit in the south of the strait, one of them a supertanker. A third was hit east of the strait. The ships' names and any casualties were not given, and there is no independent confirmation yet.
🔹 The UN told the Security Council on Friday that at least 25 seafarers have been killed in and around Hormuz since the war began in February.
🔹 Shipping through Hormuz is about 65% below pre-war levels, the UK's maritime agency (UKMTO) says. The US military says it has cleared the main routes of mines.

headline: [Historic First!] Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold [Three-Way Summit] in China
sub: Nuclear arms and Iran war on the agenda
caption:
🌍 Historic First: Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold Three-Way Summit in China

The White House said on Friday that US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, next week. It will be the first three-way meeting of the three leaders, held on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

🔹 White House spokesperson Olivia Wales said Trump will discuss "the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world". The New START nuclear treaty between the US and Russia expired in February.
🔹 US officials said the Iran war will also be discussed, but Ukraine will not. A senior US official told Reuters: "We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement."
🔹 The APEC leaders' meeting runs on 18-19 November. Moscow and Beijing had not commented when the plan was announced.

headline: [Big Ruling!] ICC Stops Probe Into Alleged Crimes by [US Troops] in Afghanistan
sub: Court will now focus on the Taliban
caption:
⚖️ Big Ruling: ICC Stops Probe Into Alleged Crimes by US Troops in Afghanistan

Judges at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague have ordered the prosecutor to stop investigating alleged crimes by American troops in Afghanistan. The ruling was issued on Thursday and made public on Friday.

🔹 The court's Afghanistan inquiry will now focus only on alleged crimes by the Taliban since 2021. A separate probe into the ISIS group in Khorasan (ISKP) was also closed.
🔹 The judges cited "significant limitations to the Prosecution's ability to conduct its investigations and secure evidence." The US troops part of the probe had been inactive since 2021.
🔹 The prosecutor's office says it has already appealed. Arrest warrants for four Taliban leaders remain in force. The US is not an ICC member and has put sanctions on court staff.

sub: India chase 338 with one wicket left
caption:
🏏 Last-Ball Thriller: India Beat Pakistan to Win U-19 Asia Cup Final

India beat Pakistan by one wicket in the Under-19 Asia Cup final in Muscat, Oman, on Saturday. India needed three runs off the very last ball, and Mohit Ulva hit a four to win the match.

🔹 Pakistan won the toss and made 337 for 9. Usman Khan scored 107, Abdul Qadir 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf 63. India's Kavya Patel took 4 wickets for 68 runs.
🔹 India chased 338 and finished on 339 for 9 in 50 overs. Mohit Ulva was not out on 49 off just 26 balls.

headline: [History Made!] SpaceX Catches Starship With Tower Arms After [14 Orbits]
sub: First catch of a Starship back from space
caption:
🚀 History Made: SpaceX Catches Starship With Tower Arms After 14 Orbits

SpaceX caught its Starship spacecraft with the giant arms of its launch tower at Starbase, Texas, on Saturday. It is the first time a Starship has been caught after returning from space. The ship landed about 22 hours after it took off on Friday.

🔹 On its 15th test flight, Starship circled Earth 14 times at about 265 km (165 miles) up and released 26 Starlink satellites.
🔹 The Super Heavy booster did not come back as planned. Its engines stopped too early and it was destroyed over the Gulf of Mexico. SpaceX is investigating.
🔹 Catching rockets is key to reusing them. NASA plans to use Starship as a Moon lander. NASA chief Jared Isaacman said: "It was almost magic."

Denmark beat Portugal 4-1 in Braga on Saturday in the UEFA Nations League. It was Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement last week.

sub: Hamas confirms death; strike hit Khan Younis
caption:
📍 Gaza Strike Israel Kills Hamas Rafah Brigade Chief Samir Abu Younis

Israel's military says it carried out a strike on Saturday that targeted a senior commander of Hamas's armed wing in Khan Younis, southern Gaza. Hamas confirmed that Samir Abu Younis, the commander of its Rafah brigade, was killed. Medics said the strike hit the Mawasi area and wounded others.

🔹 Abu Younis, 53, had been a member of Hamas's armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades, since 1991, Reuters reported.
🔹 Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire began. Five Israeli soldiers have died in the same period.

headline: [Border Shutdown!] Estonia to Close All Crossings With Russia From [December 1]
sub: Tallinn blames Russian spy agency for arson plot
caption:
🚨 BREAKING: Border Shutdown! Estonia to Close All Crossings With Russia From December 1

Estonia will close all of its border crossings with Russia from December 1, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced on Sunday. The decision comes after an attempted arson attack on Estonian drone maker Threod Systems early on Saturday, which Estonian authorities say was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence service.

🔹 Three crossings are open now, at Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa. The minister did not say how long the closure will last.
🔹 Eight people were detained over the attack, which caused only minor damage. Russia had not commented, and it has denied similar accusations in the past.
🔹 Tsahkna said: "Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences." Finland, Latvia and Lithuania have been informed.

sub: Forces pull back from Bab el-Mandeb Strait
caption:
🚨 BREAKING: Yemen War Shift! Houthis Advance to 60 km From Aden as Government Retreats

Yemen's Houthis have advanced to about 60 km (37 miles) from Aden, the temporary seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government, military and government sources told AFP on Sunday. Earlier the same day, Saudi-backed government forces said they were pulling out of areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on defending Aden.

🔹 Sources say the Houthis seized two districts in Lahj province and reached the Al-Kharaz camp, where the UN refugee agency says 9,600 refugees are at risk.
🔹 The Houthis now say they hold more than 150 km of the Red Sea coast that government forces left. Bab el-Mandeb is one of the world's most important shipping routes.
🔹 Government forces have been building sandbag defences and digging tunnels around Aden. The UN says more than 1,600 people have been killed since fighting restarted in July.

The US aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and its strike group have arrived in the Middle East, a US official told ABC News and Al Jazeera. It entered the area of US Central Command on Sunday, November 15.

England beat world champions Spain 3-2 in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday night at the Metropolitano stadium in Madrid. The result ended Spain's 43-match unbeaten run.

sub: Vulcan fails 10 minutes into flight
caption:
🚀 First-Ever Failure! ULA Rocket Loses 40 Amazon Satellites After Launch

A Vulcan rocket from United Launch Alliance (ULA), a joint company of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed after lifting off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, November 15. All 40 satellites it carried for Amazon's Leo internet network were lost.

🔹 ULA said the rocket "suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit." The cause is not yet known.
🔹 It is ULA's first full mission failure since the company was formed in 2006. It was the fifth Vulcan flight and its first in nine months.
🔹 ULA says it will investigate with its customer and return to flight as quickly as possible. NASA has offered to help. Amazon Leo is building a satellite internet network to compete with SpaceX's Starlink.

headline: [Legend Returns!] Ronaldinho, 46, Plays First Match in [11 Years]
sub: Ravenna beat Forli 2-0 in Italy
caption:
⚽ Legend Returns! Ronaldinho, 46, Plays First Match in 11 Years

Brazil legend Ronaldinho played his first official match in more than 11 years on Sunday, November 15, for Italian third-tier club Ravenna. Ravenna beat local rivals Forlì 2-0 at the sold-out Stadio Bruno Benelli.

A crash involving a fuel tanker set off a huge fire on the Ring Road in the Warraq area of Giza, part of Greater Cairo, on Wednesday evening. Egypt's Health Ministry said at least 31 people were killed and at least 21 were injured.

Rescuers have recovered at least 16 bodies from a flooded, unlicensed gold mine in the Pongkor area of Bogor, West Java, about 60 km south of Jakarta, the AP reported on Thursday. Heavy rain late on Monday made the Ciseureuh River overflow into a mine shaft about 100 metres deep.

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's request to launch up to 1 million satellites that will work as data centres in space. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr announced the decision on Wednesday, calling it "a historic first".

🔹 The satellites are "orbital compute modules": computers in space that will run AI and connect with other satellites, including SpaceX's Starlink network.

An explosion and fire hit the Bangchak oil refinery in the Phra Khanong area of eastern Bangkok, Thailand, at around 3 pm local time on Thursday. Thai authorities said at least 9 people were injured, 3 of them critically. No deaths have been reported.

🔹 Bangchak said the fire was brought under control within about 30 minutes and all production was stopped. The cause is still under investigation.

EU leaders agreed on Thursday to back Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos, 55, as the next president of the European Central Bank (ECB). French President Emmanuel Macron announced the agreement on X. He will replace France's Christine Lagarde.

An aerial projectile hit the Jazan oil refinery on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast on Thursday, killing one worker and injuring several others, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said. The worker who died was from Nepal.

The final count of New Zealand's 7 November election, released on Friday, left no group with a majority. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing bloc won 65 of the 130 seats, one seat short of the number needed to govern alone.

Turkey has completed its approval of the Mecca joint defence agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed off on the pact, and it was published in Turkey's Official Gazette on Friday. Turkey's parliament approved it earlier this month.

An airstrike hit a building in the city of al-Turbah, in Yemen's Taiz province, early on Friday. The Houthi-run health ministry said at least 11 people were killed, including children, and blamed Saudi Arabia. The toll could not be independently verified.

headline: [Landmark Ruling!] Canada's Top Court Upholds Quebec's [Religious Symbols Ban]
sub: Teachers and police barred from religious symbols
caption:
🚨 BREAKING: Landmark Ruling! Canada's Top Court Upholds Quebec's Religious Symbols Ban

Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld most of Quebec's 2019 law known as Bill 21. The law bans public school teachers, police officers and other public employees in positions of authority from wearing religious symbols at work, such as Muslim headscarves, Sikh turbans, Jewish skullcaps and Christian crosses.

🔹 The court also upheld Quebec's use of the "notwithstanding clause", which lets the province override Charter rights such as freedom of religion. The override must be renewed every five years.
🔹 The court struck down one part of the law: a rule that members of Quebec's legislature must do their work with their faces uncovered.
🔹 Quebec says the law keeps religion and government separate. Opponents say it discriminates against religious minorities, especially Muslim women who wear headscarves. The English Montreal School Board, which challenged the law, said "the advocacy continues."
